headline: Administration projects $380,000 fiscal 2027 budget shortfall as MCAS scores are presented
summary: The projection covers the full year through June 30 and assumes the $150,000 school committee contingency is used. Main causes include special education staff hired after budget approval, substitute and leave backfill, and a lower-than-planned preschool grant. The assistant superintendent's MCAS report showed 34% of grade 3 students meeting expectations in ELA. A subcommittee recommended higher pay for long-term substitutes, and two grants were accepted.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda as presented, with six yes votes read on roll call.
Approved the updated school committee operating protocols by voice vote.
Recommended to the full committee higher daily pay for long-term substitutes, effective January 1st, 2027.
Approved accepting the $25,000 FY27 Hate Crime Prevention Grant.
Approved accepting the $60,000 FY27 Massachusetts Fair Share Earmark Grant, passed unanimously.
Referred e-bike policy for school campuses to the Building and Finance subcommittee.
discussion: MCAS results: The assistant superintendent presented grade-by-grade scores, and writing was the lowest area across grades. Members asked why scores are below the state and how interventions will work, and some said MCAS does not reflect learning well.

Fiscal 2027 shortfall: Members asked whether the projection covers unemployment costs and new students, which could change it. Members said the district used much of its circuit breaker reserve this year and expects less circuit breaker money next year.

Fiscal 2028 budget timeline: The administration proposed a preliminary city budget by late December. Members worried a level-service number could be read as a budget request, and asked that it be discussed at Building and Finance first.

Bus safety: The administration offered fully illuminated stop signs at $650 to $800 per sign, about $12,000 to $15,000 for the fleet, or extended stop arms, which are not currently legal in Massachusetts. Members asked staff to report back on BusPatrol cameras, which would need police review and likely a city ordinance.
